dialogs.content: Well, why are you back? Did you get the door slammed on you by our great Vijnanapati? I'll have you know that he doesn't compromise so easily with the Pari.
You should just leave. And don't even think of getting anything more from me!
Pfft! You spilled the beans without our help every time, though!
So, about your Vijnanapati...
You tell Pyrrho of the Great Songs and Nasejuna's betrayal.
Nonsense. Utter nonsense! Our Vijnanapati is the most scholarly man I know. He would not band together with those defiled beings!
I'll bet you're just trying to mask your failure by sowing dissent.
Nice try, but your story's way out there. No way I'd fall for that!
Ugh... C'mon, we gotta think. Don't we have those notes that Nasejuna gave us?
It should still have Nasejuna's notes. Pyrrho should believe us if we give those to him!
What notes are these? You really love those tricks of yours, don't you?
You give Rene's Investigation Notes to Pyrrho.
This... This is indeed the great Vijnanapati's handwriting...
It truly was a once-in-a-lifetime thing that we gained such a knowledgeable leader, and yet he turned his back on our duties and threw his lot with the followers of the dark hollow...
*sigh* You may not know this, but we have struggled against the followers of the dark hollow for hundreds of years.
You could say that they are akin to our shadow, always attempting to taint our heritage. I have no doubt that the fall of our order to its present state cannot be separated from their plots.
But I never thought that this time, even our leader would be... Ah, a plague upon our house, this is!
No doubt Nasejuna has gone with those impure villains and now skulks with them in the shadows.
In the past, he followed Elder Aryadeva to the Akademiya, and upon returning, he was absorbed with those ancient documents.
We were people who emphasized praxis, and we found ourselves without a scholar like him for many years. I had thought that he would lead us to reform, but...
Honestly, we didn't see that one coming either.
But since this is how things have played out, I must handle that which remains to be done.
Our first priority is to appoint a new Vijnanapati. Things would go ill if someone takes advantage of this vacuum.
Well, Paimon's really not sure if you have much of a vacuum worth sneaking into now...
Indeed, and I am ashamed of it. As penance, allow me to give you these documents that Nasejuna left in my keeping. They record the various traditions of our Order.
Although I have not been able to understand it, I believe it might be of interest to you, so please, take it.
And if you should have any trouble in the future, just seek me out, and I will lend you my aid.
This wasn't your fault.
Well, you say he's different, but...
